title: Celina Jaitly Has Fired Back at Her Estranged Husband's Defamation Threats. The Custody Battle Now Spans Two Countries.
excerpt: After Peter Haag and his father sent legal notices demanding she delete her social media posts, the actress responded through Karanjawala & Co. and called the threats an attempt to silence her. An FIR, a Look Out Circular, and custody proceedings in Austrian courts have made this one of the most complex NRI divorces in recent memory.
body:
Celina Jaitly has broken her silence. The former Miss India and Bollywood actress has issued a detailed public response to defamation threats sent by her estranged husband, Austrian hotelier Peter Haag, and his father, DI Wolfgang J. Haag. The legal notices, sent on May 30 through Semwal & Co., demanded that she issue a full public apology and delete all social media posts related to their ongoing divorce and custody proceedings.

She has done neither.

## The Notices and the Response

The Haag family's legal notices invoked Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, accusing Celina of running a public smear campaign through social media, interviews, and media interactions. They alleged that her statements about domestic violence and child concealment were false and defamatory, and that they were prejudicing pending matrimonial proceedings in Austrian courts.

Celina's legal team at Karanjawala & Co. submitted a formal reply. In her public statement, a ten-slide post on social media, she called the notices "an attempt to divert attention from police complaints, lookout notices, allegations of violence, documented evidence before the competent authorities and pending before the courts."

"Speaking about my lived experiences and pursuing lawful remedies is not defamation," she wrote. She also pointed out that media attention involving their family had previously been welcomed. "For years, publicity involving our family was actively embraced, including Peter's participation in magazine covers, interviews, articles featuring our children and me — until it suited his own interests."

## The FIR and the Look Out Circular

The current dispute escalated after Celina filed an FIR at Mumbai's Versova Police Station, detailing allegations of cruelty, physical assault, and harassment against Peter Haag. Following Haag's non-cooperation with the investigation, Mumbai Police issued a Look Out Circular against the Austrian businessman.

In a separate case filed in November 2025 under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, Celina sought ₹100 crore in compensation and ₹10 lakh per month in maintenance. Through her attorneys, she alleged sustained physical, emotional, and verbal abuse throughout their fifteen-year marriage, and claimed that Haag had systematically stripped her of financial independence by restricting her professional engagements and preventing her from accessing her own earnings.

The metropolitan magistrate court in Andheri directed both parties to submit income affidavits by January 2027 and asked Haag to respond to the domestic violence complaint.

## A Marriage Across Continents

Celina and Peter married in 2011. Their life together took them across Mumbai, Dubai, Singapore, and Austria, following Haag's business assignments. They have three surviving sons: twins Winston and Viraaj, born in 2012, and Arthur, born in 2017. A fourth son, Shamsher, Arthur's twin, died shortly after birth.

The transnational dimension of this case makes it particularly complicated. Custody proceedings are pending before Austrian courts, while criminal and domestic violence cases are progressing through Indian courts. Celina's legal team has alleged that the children have been moved to an undisclosed location and that her access to them has been restricted, including limitations on phone contact.

## Why This Matters for the Diaspora

Cross-border custody battles are among the most painful and legally tangled situations NRI families face. When a marriage spans multiple jurisdictions, each country's courts can assert authority over different aspects of the dispute, creating parallel proceedings that can take years to resolve. Celina's case is a high-profile example of what thousands of NRI families navigate in silence: conflicting legal systems, questions of jurisdiction, and the practical impossibility of enforcing one country's court orders in another.

The legal framework is still catching up. India is not a signatory to the Hague Convention on International Child Abduction, which means there is no automatic mechanism to resolve custody disputes between India and Austria. Each case is litigated from scratch, in both countries, with the children caught in between.

## What Happens Next

The defamation notices have not been pursued as formal cases yet, and it remains to be seen whether the Haag family will follow through with court proceedings in India. The domestic violence case continues before the Andheri court. The FIR investigation is ongoing.

Celina's public stance has been unequivocal. "I will continue to speak about my experiences and fight for my children," she wrote. Whether the courts in Mumbai and Vienna can untangle this case faster than it escalates remains an open question.
